groups.text: It is currently 23 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Anthropic is easing its controversial data storage policy after facing pushback from enterprise customers. Since June, the company has stored all customer data from its Mythos and Fable models on its own servers for 30 days to identify new cyberattacks. Anthropic admitted this rule was unpopular and created a business risk. Under the new setup arriving this fall, that 30-day window remains, but the data will sit in the customer's cloud instead of with Anthropic. Developer Boris Cherny confirmed these plans publicly on X. Bloomberg reports that the company spent months building this system alongside more than 100 customers from regulated industries. Meanwhile, rival OpenAI is testing a different method to pair security with data control through partnerships with Microsoft and Databricks.

Australian authorities have charged a dual Russian-Australian citizen following an alleged plot involving Russian intelligence. The man, identified as 27-year-old Vladimir Teslov, allegedly traveled to Russia in October 2024 for military-style training before remaining in contact with people linked to Russian intelligence services. Investigators say Teslov then traveled to Ukraine in May 2025 and joined the Ukrainian Armed Forces. While there, he allegedly gained access to sensitive information regarding military personnel, units, locations, and operations. The Australian Federal Police allege that Teslov provided or attempted to provide this data to individuals acting on behalf of Russian intelligence, creating a direct risk to the safety of Ukrainian military personnel. If convicted of attempting to engage in intentional foreign interference, Teslov may face up to 20 years in prison. The police noted that while the investigation is ongoing, there is no evidence of any threat to Australia.

Thousands of people have died this year following severe earthquakes in Indonesia, Colombia, Peru, and Venezuela. In Venezuela, the deadliest disaster occurred on June 24th when a magnitude 7.2 quake was followed just 39 seconds later by an even stronger 7.5 shock. These double tremors devastated Caracas and the north of the country, killing more than 6,300 people. Researchers from Oregon State University used satellite data to estimate that over 58,000 buildings may have been damaged or destroyed in the impoverished nation. While the Philippines saw the strongest single event of the year with a magnitude 7.8 quake off Mindanao on June 8th, experts note that the total number of very strong quakes remains typical for the long-term average. In unrelated news from the academic community, a solo researcher and master's student is seeking advice after their first paper on multimodality was rejected at EMNLP despite receiving positive meta scores.

North Korean hackers recently targeted the Rust ecosystem in an open source software supply chain attack. According to cybersecurity firm Wiz, attackers used a legitimate maintainer's account on August 20 to push a poisoned version of arrayref, a popular utility with over 245 million downloads. The malicious package included a script designed to fetch a second-stage binary from a remote server. While the Rust Security Response Team removed the packages within 86 minutes and found no evidence of actual usage, the breach highlights a broader vulnerability in digital infrastructure. This risk extends to local government agencies that often lack the resources to defend themselves. Darshan Tiwari of Consultadd Public Services notes that over 80 percent of state and local organizations operate with fewer than five dedicated security staff. He cites one local housing authority that lost nearly a million dollars after attackers quietly rerouted a wire meant for affordable housing.

Developers are refining the technical foundations of open-source machine learning tools to better handle complex model architectures. The llama.cpp project has released an update that enables tensor split for LFM2 and LFM2MOE, a process assisted by deepseek-v4-flash. This release expands compatibility across various platforms, including Apple Silicon with KleidiAI enabled, Windows systems using CUDA 13, and several Ubuntu Linux configurations. In a separate effort to clean up core infrastructure, the PyTorch team has updated their clang-format standard to C++20. This change resolves a conflict where the system previously used the older C++17 standard, which caused the software to misinterpret concepts as pre-C++20 tokens and create formatting errors in files like MHA.cpp. While llama.cpp focuses on expanding hardware accessibility for specific models, PyTorch is addressing internal code consistency to ensure its codebase aligns with modern programming standards.

Extreme heat is taking a heavy toll on much of France's agricultural sector, but the high temperatures are creating ideal conditions for salt harvesting in Western France. In the famous salt marshes of Guérande, this summer's harvest looks set to be particularly bountiful. Meanwhile, in Africa, the World Health Organization has warned of a high risk that an Ebola epidemic could spread internationally. The outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is far from controlled and has caused more than 2,300 deaths since May. In Cameroon, 93-year-old President Paul Biya has returned to Yaoundé after spending seventy-three days in Switzerland. His long absence fueled speculation about his health and drew sharp criticism from the opposition. On a different note, Angélique Kidjo became the first African musician to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame during a ceremony in Los Angeles this past Tuesday.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority has opened a case to review a proposed sixty-seven million pound subsidy for Ryanair UK Limited. The Subsidy Advice Unit is now evaluating whether the funding, offered by Invest Northern Ireland, complies with subsidy control requirements. This particular investment aims to establish a large-scale maintenance, repair, and overhaul facility for aircraft engines in Northern Ireland to create professional and skilled jobs while reducing regional productivity disadvantages. A final report on the compliance of this capital grant and employment support is expected by October 2nd. In separate corporate news from the United States, Hepion Pharmaceuticals filed an initial statement of beneficial ownership of securities with the SEC yesterday. The filing, dated August 21st, identifies James Gordon Liddy as the reporting person for the pharmaceutical company based in Red Bank, New Jersey.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 19 and 24 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day and Höfische at seven in the evening. Your work calendar has a NAS brainstorm at one in the afternoon.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
